content:
Maya Chen: Quick thread — brought Spiral-7B up this morning. Did a focused quant smoke + unit-econ pass. can someone paste a TL;DR for product/GTN?
Samir Patel: TL;DR incoming. did int8/int4/int2 sweeps on GTN-slice-22 (50k prompts, multi-turn + summarization subset).
Samir Patel: Scorecard (summary):
```
- Spiral-7B-fp16 (baseline): p95 latency 92ms, quality 0.0 (baseline), cost ≈ $0.52 per 1k tokens
- Spiral-7B-int8: p95 84ms, quality -1.3 pts (task-avg), cost ≈ $0.15 per 1k tokens
- Spiral-7B-int4: p95 78ms, quality -3.9 pts (task-avg), cost ≈ $0.045 per 1k tokens
- Spiral-7B-int2 (experimental): p95 72ms, quality -8.1 pts, cost ≈ $0.025 per 1k tokens
Notes: KV-cache preserved across quant levels; throughput improves modestly with lower precision.
```
Eli Park: Which metric for "quality pts" here? avg accuracy across GTN QA + ROUGE for summarization?
Samir Patel: Yep — averaged normalized QA accuracy (GTN-QA) + ROUGE-L on the summ subset, then scaled to a 0..100 delta so it's human-interpretable for product. Individual tasks attached in the full artifact.
Anya Koval: Product ask: our cost ceiling for the assistant is ~ $0.12 / 1k tokens for steady-state. want a recommendation for default + fallbacks for GTN. Also need quick canary plan.
Samir Patel: Recommendation: default -> int4 for non-critical query/path to hit the cost target, fallback -> int8 for higher-fidelity/edge cases, and pinned fp16 for high-value flows (billing, legal summarization). Proposed split: 80% int4, 19% int8, 1% fp16 (gradual canary).
Maya Chen: Concern: int4 quality delta (-3.9) is visible on long multi-turn reasoning slices. Any signal where int4 fails badly?
Samir Patel: Yes — priming-sensitive, long-context chain-of-thought prompts ( > 1.5k tokens) see larger drops. Short Q&A and casual chat are fine. We flagged ~2% of slices as regressions >6 pts; those map to rare multi-step planning prompts.
Anya Koval: Ok — product decision: prefer int8 default for the assistant if user-visible regressions >2% persist. Can we do a hybrid routing heuristic?
Eli Park: Propose routing rule: if prompt length > 800 tokens OR prompt contains trigger tokens ("plan", "step-by-step"), route to int8; else serve int4. That keeps cost ~ $0.07/1k tokens effective while cutting regressions.
Samir Patel: Canary rollout snippet (ops-ready):
```yaml
rollout:
  - 5% -> Spiral-7B-int4 (canary, 24h)
  - 5% -> Spiral-7B-int8 (comparison)
  - monitor: [GTN-quality-score, longform-regression-rate, p95-latency, token-cost]
  - if longform-regression-rate > 1.5% -> pause int4 and shift +10% to int8
```
CI Bot: smoke tests passed (quant-sweep v1). artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/spiral7b/quant-sweep-v1/
Maya Chen: Next steps: Samir, can you attach per-task deltas and the small sample of failure prompts? Product wants a 1-pager for GTN.
Samir Patel: Will attach CSV + 200 failure examples by EOD. Also adding a tiny eval harness to run the routing rule locally.
Anya Koval: Perfect — that should let GTN triage. thanks team :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: Cool — closing this readout. follow-up thread for rollout metrics after 24h canary.
